chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah said: Muhammad ibn Ziyad narrated to them from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a woman who had a husband and a child from another man, and a child from her husband, when the child from the other man died, he said: 'Her husband will separate from her for three months until he knows whether there is a child in her womb or not. If there is a child in her womb, he will be inherited.'
Abu Ali said: And this is contrary to the truth and is not to be acted upon.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on inheriting a child in the womb when their uncle dies?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the procedure for determining the inheritance rights of a child in the womb (*walad al-batin*) when the father dies, specifically addressing the period of waiting (*istibra*) to confirm pregnancy. While the Imam suggests a three-month separation to ascertain if the child is from the deceased, the commentator Abu Ali critiques this as diverging from the established legal truth, highlighting the nuanced development of Shia jurisprudence regarding fetal inheritance. This reflects the broader scholarly discourse on how *istibra* periods vary based on marital status and the certainty of lineage in inheritance distribution.
